decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Miguel points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Miguel keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Miguel a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Permanent exhibition
decisions.situation: You draw a huge purple person on the wall. Miguel walks in while you are adding the teeth.

choices.label: Show off your work
Help clean it up
Blame a very tall baby

result.title: Mixed reviews
result.body: Miguel gives you paper. The wall gets a long scrub.

journal.text: I drew a purple person on the wall. It was not a commissioned piece.

decisions.title: Your name is No
decisions.situation: You decide Miguel is called “No”, because they say it so often. You introduce them to a visitor as No. No looks tired.

choices.label: Ask No for a biscuit
Ask whether their middle name is Stop
Give them their old name back

result.title: They answer to it
result.body: Miguel says no. You point out that they have just said their own name. The visitor needs a moment.

journal.text: I named Miguel No, then asked No for a biscuit.

decisions.title: An important appointment
decisions.situation: In a lift, Miguel lets you press the button for your floor. There are so many other buttons. It seems wasteful.

choices.label: Press the right button once
Ask what the other buttons do
Press a few extra floor buttons

result.title: Express service
result.body: The lift takes you where you meant to go. You have performed a valuable public service.

journal.text: I pressed the correct lift button for Miguel.

decisions.title: A mouth with sound effects
decisions.situation: Your first loose tooth makes a clicking noise. You discover you can make it louder. Lunch is about to become a performance.

choices.label: Let everyone eat in peace
Check the wobble in a mirror
Give everyone a live demonstration

result.title: A private dental matter
result.body: You leave the tooth alone. Lunch proceeds without an audience inspecting your mouth.

journal.text: I kept my loose tooth out of the lunchtime conversation.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: A nose for music
decisions.situation: Gabriel has learned to play the recorder with their nose. They ask you to accompany their debut. The first note makes everyone check for a trapped bird.

choices.label: Drum on the desk and let them have their moment
Offer to be the audience from further away
Announce that you can play an imaginary one

result.title: A very short tour
result.body: You find a beat that nearly matches the squeaks. Gabriel attempts an encore, sneezes, and announces an interval.

journal.text: I accompanied Gabriel’s nose-recorder debut by drumming on a desk.

decisions.title: Forty-two. Definitely forty-two.
decisions.situation: Helena starts a question and your hand shoots up. You have an excellent answer. You are still waiting to hear what the question is.

choices.label: Hear the rest before committing
Shout “forty-two” with total confidence
Let someone else risk it first

result.title: A useful last-minute adjustment
result.body: The question is about the number of sides on a triangle. You quietly retire forty-two and give the correct answer.

journal.text: I waited to hear a whole classroom question before answering.

decisions.title: Hostile snack takeover
decisions.situation: Gabriel offers a plain cracker for your favourite snack. They call the cracker “rare”. There are twelve more in the packet.

choices.label: Demand two snacks for your one
Eat your snack during the sales pitch
Split yours and spare the cracker

result.title: The negotiator gets greedy
result.body: Gabriel nearly agrees, then notices you smiling. They withdraw the cracker and their goodwill.

journal.text: I tried to turn Gabriel’s snack offer into a better deal for myself.

decisions.title: Little Star, big photograph
decisions.situation: Your school-photo proof arrives. You wore an old top that barely fits. Across your chest, in extremely clear letters, it says “LITTLE STAR”.

choices.label: Ask for a crop above the lettering
Sign the proof like a celebrity
Inspect everyone else’s proof for worse outfits

result.title: Now a very large head
result.body: The cropped proof removes the slogan and most of your shoulders. You approve it before anyone suggests keeping the original as a wallet photo.

journal.text: I cropped an embarrassing slogan out of my school photograph.

decisions.title: Your debut single is chemistry
decisions.situation: Gabriel secretly records you singing chemistry definitions and adds a dance beat. The file is called “Desperate for Zinc”. They want to send it to the class.

choices.label: Make them delete the recording
Demand credit as the anonymous vocalist
Record a completely unnecessary key change

result.title: An extremely limited release
result.body: Gabriel deletes it while you watch. They call you difficult. You call them a record label with no permission forms.

journal.text: I made Gabriel delete a secret recording of my chemistry revision song.

decisions.title: Immortal words, wrong person
decisions.situation: The yearbook proof puts Gabriel’s quote under your photo: “I peaked at nine.” Helena needs corrections today. You are not sure you want to ask what happened at nine.

choices.label: Return the quote to its rightful owner
Write gloriously vain quotes together
Approve it as your mysterious backstory

result.title: A corrected confession
result.body: Helena fixes the names. Gabriel explains that they won a particularly good sack race.

journal.text: I corrected swapped yearbook quotations.

decisions.title: Fastest toy car alive
decisions.situation: You invented the numbers for a marked science report. Your toy car apparently reached 90,000 kilometres an hour. Helena asks to see the original measurements.

choices.label: Admit it and take the report back
Offer a live demonstration instead
Invent a second sheet of measurements

result.title: The car has been recalled
result.body: Helena lets you submit a properly measured replacement with a reduced mark. The real car rolls under a cupboard. You record that too.

journal.text: I admitted inventing science data and replaced my report with real measurements.

decisions.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
decisions.situation: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup
Delete the post without explaining
Add “No questions. Bring gloves.”

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in São Paulo takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs R$0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about
Claim you invented motivational seminars

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in São Paulo needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in São Paulo.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: Inside the chicken
decisions.situation: The festival mascot has quit. A volunteer thrusts a chicken suit at you and offers cash for one hour. The head smells of onions. Something inside it is still warm.

choices.label: Tell them you only came for the stalls
Wear the chicken suit for R$387.20
Carry the head around and ask if anyone knows it

result.title: A civilian again
result.body: The volunteer apologises and puts the chicken head on a traffic cone. A child immediately asks the cone for a photo.

journal.text: I declined an emergency shift inside a festival chicken.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing
Send someone a proper message
Investigate another hour of success

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first
Praise how neatly it broke
Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

Admire its excellent fuel economy
Pretend to fall overboard

result.title: A surprisingly useful explanation
result.body: The guide says it is about status and imaginary ownership. The visitor looks relieved that somebody has supplied an answer.

journal.text: I asked about an invisible-yacht artwork in São Paulo.

choices.label: Play the grieving relative sincerely
Ask how real inheritance rules work
Demand the imaginary house in character

result.title: A family worth inventing
result.body: You deliver a moving line about the fictional deceased. The facilitator thanks you. Your neighbour asks whether the line helped your share.

journal.text: I played a grieving relative at an estate-planning demonstration.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Return the microphone immediately
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: Happy statistical decline
decisions.situation: For your birthday, someone sends a list of famous people who had achieved more by your age. They finish with “Hope this inspires you!”

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: You are almost in the picture

choices.label: Enjoy the unfinished little mystery
Write down what you do remember
Build a grand explanation around the pose

result.title: A life outside the frame
result.body: You let the unknown detail remain unknown. The photograph still holds an ordinary moment worth keeping.

journal.text: I enjoyed an old photograph without solving every detail.
